temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Pack says Party wings, flats and drumettes 390°F / 200°C · 22 min 400°F / 205°C · 29 min Standard split wings 390°F / 200°C · 26 min 400°F / 205°C · 35 min Jumbo or whole wings 390°F / 200°C · 30 min 400°F / 205°C · 40 min Why frozen wings cook unevenly Raw wings usually freeze into clumps in the bag. Where two wings touch, neither surface sees hot air, so that side stays pale and the meat beneath lags behind. The skin has a second problem: frozen wings carry ice, and the water it releases has to leave before the fat under the skin can render and crisp. Prise the wings apart with tongs at the first shake, spread them out, and let the second shake turn them so every side gets its turn near the fan. Worked example: a bag of raw frozen wings A bag of raw split wings says to bake from frozen at 400°F for 35 minutes. In a basket air fryer that becomes 390°F for 26 minutes. Preheat 4 minutes, tip in a single layer, and shake twice; at the first shake, separate any wings that are still frozen together. Party-size flats and drumettes finish in about 22 minutes, jumbo wings in about 30. Toss them in sauce after cooking, not before, or the sugar burns long before the meat is safe. How to tell they are done Raw wings must reach 165°F (74°C) next to the bone, so check the thickest drumette with a thermometer; the skin can brown while the middle is still cold. Many people take wings further for a more tender texture. The skin should be crisp and blistered, with no soft, pale patches where wings were touching. Before they go in Read the bag first: raw and fully cooked wings look alike but need different settings. Skip the oil; the skin has plenty of its own fat. Season with a dry rub once they are separated at the first shake, so it sticks to the thawed surface. Related presets Frozen fries 400°F · 15 min · shake ×2 Frozen chicken breast 360°F · 24 min · flip at 12 Frozen chicken nuggets 400°F · 10 min · shake ×1 400°F oven to air fryer, every food → Frozen pack converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long do raw frozen wings take in the air fryer? About 26 minutes at 390°F, shaken 2 times, until they reach 165°F. Small party wings take about 22 minutes and jumbo wings about 30. What about fully cooked or sauced frozen wings? They only need heating through, not cooking: about 12 minutes at 380°F (195°C), shaken once. They were cooked at the factory, so there is no raw-chicken risk; stop when the sauce is bubbling and sticky. Do I need to thaw wings before air frying? No. The setting above is for wings straight from the freezer. Just separate them at the first shake. When should I add sauce? After cooking. Toss the hot wings in sauce in a bowl, then return them for a minute or two if you want it to set. Can I use the fresh-wing setting for frozen wings? No. Fresh wings cook faster and hotter; frozen ones need the extra time for the ice to clear and the centre to come up to temperature.
